I have farmed in Quzhou County for a long time, and on 9 mu with well irrigation I will keep the land in the pattern that is most stable for me: most of the farm in the wheat-maize rotation, and a smaller piece in cotton. I am not trying to be experimental this year. I have enough experience and education to manage improved seed, timely fertilization, and irrigation carefully, and I prefer a plan that protects yield without creating too much labor pressure for a two-person household. I will put 6 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, because that fits my existing system and makes the best use of irrigated land. I will keep 3 mu in cotton because it still diversifies income and spreads risk. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate-high nitrogen, balanced phosphorus and potassium, and three irrigations because water is available and wheat responds well here. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer relatively strong, irrigate in key stages, and control pests with a few targeted sprays. For cotton, I will stay more cautious on area, use hybrid seed, give it enough potassium, irrigate several times from squaring to boll filling, and expect more pest management work than for grain crops. I will use rotary tillage on the wheat-maize land for speed and practicality, and plough the cotton field because I want a cleaner, deeper seedbed there.
